question: The Survey of English Dialects, run from 1950 to 1961, chose whom to record in each village?
options: A random sample of adult residents
Elderly men who had rarely moved
answer: Elderly men who had rarely moved. Fieldworkers sought people over 60, born locally, often farm workers, in 313 mostly rural places, to catch the oldest forms before they vanished; linguists later called the type NORMs, non-mobile older rural males. The maps show a countryside of grandfathers, with most towns left out.
move: Before trusting a map of how people speak, ask who was asked.
ask: Before I trust a survey about people, who did they actually ask?
trap: Assuming a national survey recorded a fair cross-section of the nation.
reference: Chambers & Trudgill, Dialectology, 2nd ed., Cambridge University Press, 1998
